title: Typed response envelope
description: The typed view a caller consumes, carried alongside the lossless raw payload (R8). Every later layer reads this rather than a raw HTTP response, so a field added here is a field the loop can reason about; a field omitted is invisible. `reasoning_content` is therefore explicit rather than dropped.

finish_reason.description: null is possible on a truncated stream and must stay distinguishable from a completed turn -- an absent reason is not a successful stop. Observed values on this provider: stop and tool_calls.

content.description: A tool-call turn reports an empty STRING here, not null, and the distinction is preserved rather than normalized: the fidelity oracle re-serializes the typed view and compares it against the captured bytes, so collapsing '' to null would make a faithful response look unfaithful.

reasoning_content.description: Captured explicitly, and replayed: U1 pinned this against the live provider, and the rule is stronger than 'replay it when asked'. An assistant tool-call turn that omits it is refused with a 400 when the provider does not recognize the tool_call id, and accepted when it does -- so the requirement depends on server-side state a client cannot inspect. The only implementable rule is to always send it back.

system_fingerprint.description: The provider's backend-build identifier, present on every captured success. Retained because it is the one field that explains a behaviour change between two runs of the same bytes against the same model id: without it, a shift looks like the model becoming worse, and with it, there is a name for what changed.

arguments.description: Kept as the provider's raw argument string, never re-serialized: re-encoding would silently normalize escapes and key order, and the fidelity oracle compares these bytes.
